title: Typed fragment commit protocol and graceful tool degradation — acceptance criteria
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Background: We need a clear, testable acceptance for how typed streaming fragments are committed and how the system handles tool/function call failures during a stream. Current contracts allow partial fragments and tool envelopes, but do not mandate a deterministic commit marker or a standardized failure classification that callers and gateways can rely on.

Goals:
- Define a minimal commit protocol for typed frames that signals finality of an emitted object across streamed responses.
- Specify tool-call failure modes and a standard fallback envelope so downstream integrations (tool gateway, console, SDKs) can render deterministic state and retry behavior.
- Surface observability and test steps so SRE/QA can validate behavior under normal and degraded network conditions.

Scope:
- In scope: streaming typed frames (JSON/text frames with schema_id), tool invocation envelopes inside streams, failure classification (transient/permanent/retryable), commit marker semantics, trace propagation, telemetry hooks.
- Out of scope: model-level fallback policy design (which alternate model to use) and CLI client changes. Those will be separate follow-ups.

Acceptance summary: Must provide a compact commit envelope, a standardized failure object with failure_class and suggested_backoff_ms, and guarantee that when a commit is emitted any consumer replaying the stream can deterministically assemble the final object. Telemetry must include trace_id, emit_seq, and tool_invocation_id for each tool call event.
acceptance_criteria: Typed frames: Every streamed typed frame must include headers: schema_id (string), emit_seq (int as string), trace_id (string). Example header line: "schema_id:redwood.v1.order". The schema_id must be a registered catalog value or a detectable version hash.

Commit marker: Streams that intend to produce a final typed object must emit a final frame with header commit:true and commit_seq equal to the highest emit_seq. Consumers must be able to wait for commit:true to treat the object as final. If a stream ends without commit:true, the object is considered partial and must be annotated as partial=true in the SDK envelope.

Idempotent replays: Replaying the same stream (same trace_id and emit_seq sequence) must result in identical assembled object when all frames are present; SDK should deduplicate frames by (trace_id, emit_seq).

Tool invocation envelope: Tool calls in-stream must use an explicit tool-invoke frame with fields: tool_invocation_id, tool_name, args_schema_id. The engine must emit a corresponding tool-result frame with matching tool_invocation_id when available.

Failure classification: Tool-result frames representing failures must include failure_class with one of: "transient", "permanent", "retryable" and a suggested_backoff_ms (integer as string). Example failure result: {"tool_invocation_id":"t-123","failure_class":"transient","suggested_backoff_ms":"500"}.

Graceful degradation: On tool timeouts or upstream gateway failures, the runtime must emit a fallback frame within 250ms of the timeout detection indicating fallback_type (e.g., "model-fallback", "null-ack") and include human_reason string. Consumers must be able to display a deterministic degraded UI state when fallback_type is present.

Backpressure & ordering: emit_seq must be strictly increasing for frames belonging to the same logical object. The runtime must handle transient reordering by using emit_seq to reorder before commit. Batched frames may arrive out of wire order but must be reorderable by emit_seq.

Telemetry: For every tool-invoke and tool-result pair the runtime must emit a metric event containing trace_id, tool_invocation_id, outcome (success/failure), failure_class if present, latency_ms, and node_id (serving host). These must be available to the Console within retention window for the release.

Observability traces: Trace propagation rules: incoming requests to Redwood must accept X-Redwood-Trace or generate a new trace_id. All emitted frames must carry trace_id. If a tool gateway emits its own trace, it should be attached via tool_trace_id in the tool-result frame.

Backward compatibility: If a caller does not understand commit:true, SDKs must expose a partial stream API and annotate finality only when commit:true is seen. This ensures older SDKs can still display partial results rather than failing parsing.
test_steps: Unit: serializer/deserializer roundtrip tests for frames -> ensure schema_id and emit_seq preserved across encode/decode.
Integration: end-to-end stream where model emits 6 frames including two tool-invokes; verify ordering, dedup, and final object after commit:true. Compare assembled JSON with golden fixture.

Failure injection: simulate tool gateway returning intermittent 502s and timeouts. Assert that tool-result frames with failure_class=transient are emitted and suggested_backoff_ms present, and that a fallback frame is emitted within 250ms.

Load: 1000 concurrent streaming sessions with mixed sizes; assert no more than 1% of sessions end without commit:true under normal conditions and that telemetry shows tool-failure rates below threshold for non-degraded nodes.
SDK behavior: Older SDK (no commit handling) should surface partial=true for streams ending without commit:true; updated SDK should treat commit:true as final and trigger onCommit callbacks.
Chaos: drop random middle frames on network layer and ensure consumer uses emit_seq to repair when retransmit occurs; final assembly must match golden when frames are restored.
notes: Design trade-offs: We intentionally pick a small commit envelope (single header commit:true) to minimize stream overhead vs. heavyweight two-phase commit which increases latency and complexity.

Follow-ups: Separate ticket required to standardize schema registry lookup semantics (how we resolve schema_id -> validation rules) and to add SDK helpers for automatic backoff based on suggested_backoff_ms.
UX: PM -> Design to define fallback messaging templates for common fallback_type values (model-fallback, null-ack, cached-response).
Security: commit marker and tool headers do not contain sensitive customer PII; if tool args include secrets they must be KMS-protected per private deployment guidelines.
